points.en: **Hart, 'Being'.** Q: What is the wonder that philosophy begins with? A: Not curiosity about some missing fact, but amazement that anything exists at all. Existence is an **ontological** mystery, not merely an **aetiological** (causal) one, so no purely physical explanation can answer it.
points.zh: **哈特（Hart）'Being'** 问：哲学开始于惊奇（**wonder**），这种惊奇到底是什么？答：不是对缺少的某个事实的好奇，而是对“竟然有东西存在”的惊讶。存在是存在论的（**ontological**）之谜，不只是因果的（**aetiological**）之谜，所以任何单纯物理的解释都回答不了。

points.en: **Argument:** what a thing is (its essence) does not explain that it is (its existence), so the world is absolutely contingent: it could have been otherwise, or not have existed at all. Physical causes only explain one contingent thing by another, even back to the initial singularity. Taylor's sphere: we would ask why a strange sphere is in the forest, and the same question fits a stone, a tree, or a sphere as big as the universe.
points.zh: 论证：一个东西“是什么”（本质）解释不了它“存在着”（存在），所以世界是绝对偶然的（**absolute contingency**）：本来可以是别的样子，也可以根本不存在。物理原因只是用一个偶然之物解释另一个，一直追到初始奇点也一样。泰勒（**Richard Taylor**）的圆球：在森林里发现一个奇怪的圆球，我们会问它为什么在那儿；同样的问题也适用于一块石头、一棵树，或者一个像宇宙那么大的圆球。

points.en: **Don't confuse:** contingent does not mean random or unimportant. Hart does not prove that God exists: he says reason must keep asking the question of God, and the excerpt breaks off mid-sentence.
points.zh: 别搞错：“偶然”不是“随机”或“不重要”的意思。哈特没有证明上帝存在，他只说理性必须一再追问上帝的问题（**the question of God**）；节选在半句话处就断了。

points.en: **Russell, 'The Value of Philosophy'.** Q: What is philosophy worth if it cannot give definite answers? A: Its value is **indirect**, through its effects on the lives of those who study it, and it lies only among the goods of the mind, largely in its very uncertainty. We study philosophy for its questions, not for definite answers.
points.zh: **罗素（Bertrand Russell）'The Value of Philosophy'** 问：哲学给不出确定的答案，那它有什么价值？答：它的价值是间接的（**indirect value**），通过它对学习者生活的影响实现，只在心灵的好处之中，而且很大程度上就在它的不确定性里。学哲学是为了它的问题，不是为了确定的答案。

points.en: **Argument:** without philosophy, a person is shut in by the prejudices of common sense, of his age and of his nation. Philosophy cannot tell us with certainty what the true answers are, but it suggests many possibilities and frees our thinking from the **tyranny of custom**: it lessens our certainty about what things are and increases our knowledge of what they may be.
points.zh: 论证：没有哲学的人被关在常识、时代和国家的偏见里。哲学不能确定地告诉我们真正的答案是什么，却能提出许多可能性，把思想从习俗的暴政（**tyranny of custom**）中解放出来：它减少我们对“事物是什么”的确定感，增加我们对“事物可能是什么”的知识。

points.en: **Don't confuse:** uncertainty is not philosophy's only value. Perhaps its chief value comes from contemplation: the greatness of the not-Self enlarges the Self and makes us **citizens of the universe**, while self-assertion blocks this growth.
points.zh: 别搞错：不确定性不是哲学唯一的价值。它也许最主要的价值来自沉思：非我的伟大扩大了自我（**Self and not-Self**），让我们成为宇宙公民（**citizens of the universe**）；自我主张会阻碍这种成长。

points.en: **Also know:** to a great extent, philosophy's uncertainty is more apparent than real: once a field can give definite knowledge, it becomes a separate science, as astronomy and psychology did, so what is still called philosophy is the **residue** of questions not yet answerable.
points.zh: 另外：哲学的不确定性在很大程度上只是表面的：一门学问一旦能得到确定的知识，就成了独立的科学（天文学、心理学都是这样），留下来仍叫“哲学”的是还答不了的剩余问题（**residue**）。

points.en: **Plato, Apology.** Q: What is Socrates' wisdom, and why will he not stop questioning people? A: His only wisdom is **human wisdom**: he does not think he knows what he does not know. Questioning people is his service to the god, and he will not give up philosophy even facing death, because 'the unexamined life is not worth living'.
points.zh: **柏拉图（Plato）Apology（申辩篇）** 问：苏格拉底（**Socrates**）的智慧是什么？他为什么不肯停止盘问别人？答：他唯一的智慧是人的智慧（**human wisdom**）：不以为自己知道自己不知道的事。盘问别人是在为神服务；哪怕面对死刑他也不放弃哲学，因为“未经审视的人生不值得过”。

points.en: **Argument (the oracle):** the oracle at Delphi said no one is wiser than Socrates. Knowing he was not wise, he questioned politicians, poets and craftsmen: each thought he knew important things but did not (the craftsmen did know their crafts). So Socrates is wiser only in this: he does not think he knows what he does not know. The oracle probably means that human wisdom has little or no value.
points.zh: 论证（神谕）：德尔斐（**Delphi**）神谕说没有人比苏格拉底更有智慧。他知道自己并不智慧，于是去盘问政治家、诗人和工匠，发现每个人都以为自己懂重要的事，其实不懂（工匠确实懂自己的手艺）。所以他只在一点上更智慧：不以为自己知道自己不知道的事。神谕的意思大概是：人的智慧价值很小，甚至没有。

points.en: **Don't confuse:** human wisdom is not 'I know that I know nothing'. That slogan is not in the text, and Socrates does claim to know some things, for example that doing wrong and disobeying a superior, god or man, is shameful. Fearing death is thinking you know what you do not know, since no one knows whether death is the greatest good.
points.zh: 别搞错：人的智慧不是“我知道我一无所知”（**I know that I know nothing**），这句口号不在文本里；苏格拉底还明确说自己知道一些事，比如做错事、不服从上级（神或人）是可耻的。怕死就是以为自己知道自己不知道的事，因为没人知道死是不是最大的好事。

points.en: **Plato, Euthyphro.** Q: What is **piety**? Socrates wants the one **form** that makes every pious act pious, not a list of examples. A: None is found: each of Euthyphro's definitions fails, and he leaves in a hurry.
points.zh: **柏拉图 Euthyphro（游叙弗伦篇）** 问：什么是虔敬（**piety**）？苏格拉底要的是让所有虔敬行为都虔敬的那一个型（**form**），不是举例子。答：没有找到：游叙弗伦（**Euthyphro**）的定义一个个失败，他说有急事就走了。

points.en: **Argument (10a):** do the gods love the pious for being pious, or does their love make it pious? Euthyphro agrees they love it because it is pious. But what is god-loved is god-loved because the gods love it. So the pious and the **god-loved** are not the same: being loved by all the gods is only an affect or quality of the pious, not its nature. Outside the reading: this is usually called the **Euthyphro dilemma**.
points.zh: 论证（10a 的问题）：神爱虔敬的东西，是因为它虔敬，还是因为神爱它，它才虔敬？游叙弗伦同意：神爱它是因为它虔敬。可为神所爱的（**god-loved**）之所以为神所爱，是因为神爱它。所以虔敬和为神所爱的不是一回事：被所有神爱只是虔敬的一种遭受或性质，不是它的本质。补充（读物外）：这个问题通常叫“游叙弗伦困境”（**Euthyphro dilemma**）。

points.en: **Don't confuse the failed definitions:** (1) prosecuting wrongdoers, as Euthyphro is doing to his father: one example, not a form; (2) what the gods love: the gods disagree, so one act could be both pious and impious; (3) what all the gods love: refuted by the 10a argument. Then care of the gods, service to the gods, and a kind of trading with the gods, which circles back to what the gods love.
points.zh: 别搞错几个失败的定义：①起诉做错事的人（游叙弗伦正在告自己的父亲）：只是一个例子，不是型；②神所喜爱的：诸神意见不合，同一个行为可能既虔敬又不虔敬；③所有神都爱的：被 10a 的论证驳倒。后面还有照料神、服侍神、与神交易，最后又绕回“神所喜爱的”。

points.en: **Plato, Meno.** Q: Can **virtue** be taught? Socrates says we must first know what virtue is. A: Apparently not, since no teachers of virtue can be found; virtue itself is never defined. On the way, a key distinction emerges: **knowledge** is **true opinion** tied down by an **account of the reason why**.
points.zh: **柏拉图（Plato）Meno（美诺篇）** 问：美德（**virtue**）能教吗？苏格拉底（**Socrates**）说得先知道美德是什么。答：看来不能，因为找不到教美德的老师；美德本身也始终没有被定义。途中得出一个关键区分：知识（**knowledge**）是被对原因的说明（**account of the reason why**）拴住的真意见（**true opinion**）。

points.en: **Argument (the debater's argument and recollection):** you cannot search for what you know (you already have it) or for what you do not know (you would not know what to look for), so inquiry seems impossible. Socrates replies that the soul is immortal and has learned everything, so searching and learning are **recollection**. The slave boy, never taught geometry, is led by questions to see that the square on the diagonal has double the area.
points.zh: 论证（辩论家的论证与回忆说）：已经知道的不必找，不知道的又不知道要找什么，所以探究似乎不可能。苏格拉底回答：灵魂不朽，早已学过一切，所以寻找和学习就是回忆（**recollection**）。从没学过几何的奴隶男孩，在提问的引导下看出：以原正方形的对角线为边的正方形，面积正好是原来的两倍。

points.en: **Larissa and Daedalus:** someone with a correct opinion about the road to **Larissa** guides as well as someone who knows it. True opinions are like the statues of **Daedalus**: they run away unless tied down, and tying them down with an account of the reason why turns them into knowledge. So knowledge is worth more because it is stable, not because it gets better results.
points.zh: 去拉里萨的路和代达罗斯的雕像：对去拉里萨（**Larissa**）的路有正确看法的人，带路不比认识路的人差。真意见像代达罗斯（**Daedalus**）的雕像，不拴住就会溜走；用对原因的说明拴住，它就变成知识。所以知识更值钱是因为稳定，不是因为结果更好。

points.en: **Don't confuse:** the boy ends with true opinions, not yet knowledge; repeated questioning would turn them into knowledge. The ending, that virtue comes to good people as a gift from the gods, is only conditional: to know it clearly, we must first learn what virtue itself is. Outside the reading: the debater's argument is usually called **Meno's paradox**.
points.zh: 别搞错：男孩最后只有真意见，还不是知识，要反复提问才会变成知识。结尾说美德是神的赐予，这只是有条件的结论：要清楚地知道，得先弄清美德本身是什么。补充（读物外）：辩论家的论证（**debater's argument**）通常叫“美诺悖论”（**Meno's paradox**）。

title.zh: 笛卡尔论怀疑与确定性

points.en: **Descartes, Meditations 1-2.** Q: Can he find one thing that is completely certain, to build lasting knowledge on? A: Yes. Even if all his old beliefs can be doubted, 'I am, I exist' is necessarily true each time he asserts it or conceives it. He is a **thinking thing**, and his mind is known more easily and more evidently than any body.
points.zh: **笛卡尔（René Descartes）Meditations 第一、第二沉思** 问：能不能找到一样完全确定的东西，在上面建立长久的知识？答：能。就算旧信念全都可以怀疑，每当他说出或想到“我在，我存在”，它就必然为真。他是一个思维之物（**thinking thing**），他的心灵比任何物体都更容易、更明显地被认识。

points.en: **Argument (the doubts, step by step):** (1) the senses sometimes deceive, but only about very small or distant things; (2) dreaming: there is no sure sign to tell waking from sleeping, so even his belief that he has hands is doubtful, though arithmetic and geometry still seem certain; (3) a **deceiving God**, or a weaker cause, could make him wrong even about 2 + 3 = 5. The **malicious demon** then helps him resist habit: it is a method, not something he believes.
points.zh: 论证（怀疑一层层加强）：①感官有时会骗人，但只够得着很小或很远的东西；②做梦：没有可靠的标志能区分醒和睡，所以连“我有手”都可疑，但算术和几何似乎仍然确定；③骗人的上帝（**deceiving God**），或者更弱的原因，可以让他连 2 + 3 = 5 都算错。之后的恶魔（**malicious demon**）是用来对抗习惯的方法，不是他相信的东西。

points.en: **'I am' and the wax:** even a supremely powerful deceiver must be deceiving someone, so he exists whenever he thinks. Subtracting everything that needs a body leaves only thinking, so strictly he is only a thing that thinks. Wax by the fire changes all its sensed qualities but is still the same wax, so its nature is grasped by the mind alone, through **purely mental scrutiny**.
points.zh: “我在”和蜡块：再强的骗子也得骗某个人，所以只要他在思考，他就存在。减掉一切需要身体的东西，只剩下思维，所以严格地说他只是一个在思考的东西。蜡块放到火边，所有感觉到的性质都变了，却还是同一块蜡，所以它的本性只由心灵把握，靠的是纯粹心灵的审视（**purely mental scrutiny**）。

points.en: **Don't confuse:** the dreaming argument does not say he is dreaming now. Arithmetic is doubted through the deceiving God; the demon passage never mentions it. 'I think, therefore I am' is not in this reading, and Meditation 2 does not prove that mind and body are different things.
points.zh: 别搞错：梦境论证没说他现在就在做梦；让算术也变得可疑的是骗人的上帝，恶魔那一段没有提到算术；“我思故我在”（**I think, therefore I am**）这句话不在这份读物里；第二沉思也没有证明心灵和身体是两种不同的东西。

points.en: **Russell, The Problems of Philosophy, Ch. 1.** Q: Is any knowledge so certain that no reasonable person could doubt it? A: We must separate **appearance** from **reality**: in sensation we directly know only **sense-data**, such as the colours we see and the hardness we feel; the real table, if there is one, is a **physical object** that is not seen but inferred.
points.zh: **罗素（Bertrand Russell）The Problems of Philosophy 第 1 章** 问：有没有一种知识确定到任何讲理的人都无法怀疑？答：要分清表象与实在（**appearance and reality**）：在感觉中我们直接知道的只有感觉材料（**sense-data**），比如看到的颜色、摸到的硬度；真实的桌子（如果有的话）是物理对象（**physical object**），看不到，只能推出来。

points.en: **Argument:** the table's colour, shape and texture change with the viewpoint, the light and the viewer, and no one appearance has a better claim than the others to be the real one. Two questions remain: is there any **matter** at all? If so, what is it?
points.zh: 论证：桌子的颜色、形状、质地会随角度、光线和看的人而变，没有理由只认其中一种是“真的”。留下两个问题：到底有没有物质（**matter**）？如果有，它是什么？

points.en: **Russell, Ch. 2.** Q: Does the table exist when no one sees it? Could life be one long dream? A: The dream hypothesis cannot be refuted, but independent objects explain our experience more simply. Example: a cat gets hungry while no one is watching it, but patches of colour do not get hungry.
points.zh: **罗素第 2 章** 问：没人看的时候桌子还在吗？人生会不会是一场梦？答：梦境假说驳不倒，但“外面有独立存在的东西”能更简单地解释经验。例子：猫没人看着也会变饿，一块块颜色是不会饿的。

points.en: **Don't confuse:** Russell does not prove that the external world exists. Belief in it is an **instinctive belief**, and there is no reason to reject an instinctive belief unless it clashes with others. He also corrects Descartes: what is certain is that a brown colour is being seen, not that a lasting 'I' is seeing it.
points.zh: 别搞错：罗素没有证明外部世界存在。相信有外部世界是一种本能信念（**instinctive belief**），本能信念只有和别的本能信念冲突时，才有理由放弃。他还修正了笛卡尔（**René Descartes**）：真正确定的是“有一块棕色正被看见”，而不是“有一个一直存在的我在看”。

points.en: **van Inwagen, 'Objectivity'.** Q: Is there **objective truth**? A: Yes. A statement is true because the world really is the way it says, and the way the world is mostly does not depend on what we think. He is a **Realist** (capital R).
points.zh: **范·因瓦根（Peter van Inwagen）'Objectivity'** 问：有没有客观真理（**objective truth**）？答：有。一句话为真，是因为世界真是那样，而世界的样子大体不取决于我们怎么想。他是大写的实在论者（**Realist**）。

points.en: **Argument:** (1) the geological argument: Mount Everest would be just as high even if no minds had ever existed; (2) **anti-Realism** seems to refute itself: denying objective truth, it needs a substitute standard, but every substitute proposed so far seems to be one that anti-Realism itself lacks.
points.zh: 论证：①地质论证：就算从来没有任何心灵，珠峰（**Mount Everest**）也一样高；②反实在论（**anti-Realism**）看来会自我反驳：它否认客观真理，就得找个替代标准，可到目前为止提出的每个替代标准，看来它自己都不具备。

points.en: **Don't confuse:** lowercase realism is opposed to **idealism** (is everything mental?); capital-R Realism is opposed to anti-Realism (is there objective truth?). An idealist can still be a Realist. Conventions fix what 'Mount Everest' and 'height' refer to, not how high the mountain is.
points.zh: 别搞错：小写的实在论（**realism**）对唯心论（**idealism**），问是不是一切都是心灵的；大写的实在论（**Realism**）对反实在论，问有没有客观真理。唯心论者也可以是大写的实在论者。约定只决定“珠峰”“高度”这些词指什么，不决定那座山有多高。

points.en: **Hume, Enquiry, Sections 4-5.** Q: What grounds our beliefs that go beyond what our senses and memory show us now, such as that the sun will rise tomorrow? A: Not reasoning but custom. First, two kinds: **relations of ideas**, such as mathematics, whose denial is a contradiction, and **matters of fact**, whose opposite is always conceivable.
points.zh: **休谟（David Hume）Enquiry 第 4–5 节** 问：超出眼前感官和记忆的事（比如明天太阳会升起），我们凭什么相信？答：不是靠推理，而是靠习惯。先分两类：观念的关系（**relations of ideas**，比如数学，否定它就矛盾）和实际的事情（**matters of fact**，反面也想得出来）。

points.en: **Argument:** such reasoning rests on **cause and effect**, which we learn only from experience, never **a priori**: Adam could not tell that water would suffocate him. Reasoning from experience assumes that the future will resemble the past. That cannot be shown by demonstration, since a change in the course of nature is no contradiction, and proving it from experience would be circular.
points.zh: 论证：这类推理都靠因果（**cause and effect**），而因果只能从经验学到，不能先验（**a priori**）推出：亚当（**Adam**）第一次看到水，推不出水会让他窒息。从经验推将来，要先假定“未来会像过去”，这个假定却证明不了：证明推理不行，因为设想自然进程改变并不矛盾；用经验去证明，又是兜圈子。

points.en: **Sceptical solution:** what moves us to infer is not reason but **custom or habit**: 'Custom, then, is the great guide of human life.' Belief differs from fiction only in feeling: the same idea, conceived in a more lively, firm and steady way.
points.zh: 怀疑论式的解决（**sceptical solution**）：让我们做推论的不是理性，是习惯（**custom or habit**）：“习惯是人生的伟大向导。”信念和虚构的区别只在感受：同一个内容，被更生动、更牢固、更稳定地构想。

points.en: **Don't confuse:** Hume never says we should stop trusting experience (as an agent, he is quite satisfied); he says only that the inference does not come from reasoning. Outside the reading: 'the problem of induction' (this week's syllabus title) and 'Hume's fork' are later labels that Hume never uses.
points.zh: 别搞错：休谟没说不该相信经验（作为行动者他完全满意），他只说这种推论不是靠推理来的。补充（读物外）：“归纳问题”（**the problem of induction**，本周课程大纲的标题）和“休谟之叉”（**Hume's fork**）都是后人的叫法，休谟原文里没有。

points.en: **Goodman, 'The New Riddle of Induction'.** Q: Which hypotheses are confirmed by their instances? A: Only **lawlike** ones. A piece of copper that conducts electricity supports 'all copper conducts electricity', but one man in this room being a third son does not support 'all men now in this room are third sons'. Nothing yet tells us what makes a hypothesis lawlike; Goodman calls this problem the **new riddle of induction**.
points.zh: **古德曼（Nelson Goodman）'The New Riddle of Induction'** 问：哪些假说能被它的实例确证（**confirmation**）？答：只有似律的（**lawlike**）假说能。一块铜导电，支持“所有铜都导电”；房间里一个男人是第三子，却不支持“现在房间里所有男人都是第三子”。可到目前为止，没有什么告诉我们是什么让一个假说成为似律的；古德曼把这个问题叫作归纳的新谜题（**new riddle of induction**）。

points.en: **Argument (grue):** something is **grue** if it is examined before t and green, or not examined before t and blue. Every emerald examined before t is green, so it is also grue. By a definition of confirmation that looks only at form, the same evidence supports 'all emeralds are green' and 'all emeralds are grue' equally, yet they predict different colours for emeralds examined after t.
points.zh: 论证（**grue**）：在 t 之前被检查过并且是绿的，或者没在 t 之前被检查过并且是蓝的，就叫 grue。t 之前检查过的祖母绿都是绿的，所以也都是 grue 的。按只看形式的确证定义，同样的证据同等支持“所有祖母绿都是绿的”和“所有祖母绿都是 grue 的”，可两者对 t 之后才检查的祖母绿预测的颜色不同。

points.en: **Don't confuse:** Goodman agrees that grue is ill-behaved (not fit for lawlike hypotheses), but not because it mentions a time: starting from grue and **bleen**, green has to be defined with a time too (symmetry). The excerpt ends without an answer, and it never mentions Hume.
points.zh: 别搞错：古德曼也认为 grue 是表现不好的（**ill-behaved**）谓词，不能用在似律假说里，但原因不在它提到了时间：从 grue 和 **bleen** 出发，green 也要用时间来定义（两边对称）。节选到最后也没给答案，而且根本没提休谟。

points.en: **Nagel, 'What Is It Like to Be a Bat?'** Q: Can consciousness be explained by physical **reduction**? A: Not by any kind of reduction we now have, because reductive analyses leave out the **subjective character of experience**: an organism is conscious just when 'there is something that it is like to be that organism', for the organism itself.
points.zh: **内格尔（Thomas Nagel）'What Is It Like to Be a Bat?'** 问：意识能用物理还原（**reduction**）来解释吗？答：现有的任何一种还原都做不到，因为还原式的分析都漏掉了经验的主观特征（**subjective character of experience**）：一个生物有意识，当且仅当做这个生物“是有某种样子的”，而且是对它自己而言。

points.en: **Argument:** bats perceive by **echolocation**; we can only partly imagine what it would be like for us to behave like a bat, and that still does not tell us what being a bat is like for the bat itself. Successful reductions move away from a particular **point of view** toward objectivity (as when sound is understood as waves), but experience is tied to its point of view, so each step toward objectivity takes us further from it.
points.zh: 论证：蝙蝠靠回声定位（**echolocation**）感知；我们只能有限地想象“我”像蝙蝠那样行动会怎样，而这仍然说明不了做蝙蝠对蝙蝠自己来说是什么样子。成功的还原要离开某个观点（**point of view**）、变得更客观，比如把声音理解成波；可经验离不开它的观点，所以每往客观走一步，就离它更远一步。

points.en: **Don't confuse:** Nagel does not say **physicalism** is false; he says we cannot yet understand how it could be true. He suggests developing an **objective phenomenology**.
points.zh: 别搞错：内格尔没说物理主义（**physicalism**）是错的，他说的是我们现在还理解不了它怎么可能是对的。他提议发展一种客观现象学（**objective phenomenology**）。

points.en: **Chalmers, 'Uploading and Consciousness'.** Q: Will I survive uploading? This splits into two questions: will an upload be conscious, and will it be me? A: An upload that is a **functional isomorph** of my brain is probably conscious; whether it would be me is a separate question.
points.zh: **查默斯（David Chalmers）'Uploading and Consciousness'** 问：我能在上传中存活吗？这拆成两个问题：上传体（**upload**）会有意识吗？它会是我吗？答：作为我大脑功能同构体（**functional isomorph**）的上传体很可能有意识；它是不是我，是另一个问题。

points.en: **Argument (gradual uploading):** replace the brain one small part at a time with computational duplicates, so behaviour and reports never change. Then consciousness either vanishes suddenly, fades gradually, or stays. Total loss from one tiny change and badly faded experience with unchanged behaviour are both implausible, so it stays. Chalmers adds that extending this reasoning strongly suggests that consciousness is an **organizational invariant**: what matters is how the parts are organized, not what they are made of.
points.zh: 论证（逐步上传，**gradual uploading**）：每次只把大脑的一小部分换成功能一样的计算部件，行为和报告始终不变。那么意识要么突然消失，要么逐渐褪色，要么一直都在。换掉一个小部件就全没了，或者经验严重褪色而行为照旧，都说不通，所以一直都在。查默斯还说，把这个推理再往前推，强烈提示意识是组织不变量（**organizational invariant**）：只看各部分怎么组织，不看是什么材料做的。

points.en: **Don't confuse:** this answers only whether the upload is conscious, not whether it would be me (**personal identity**). Destructive uploading may mean survival, or death plus a replica; the excerpt stops before Chalmers gives his own answer.
points.zh: 别搞错：这只回答了上传体有没有意识，没回答它是不是我（人格同一性，**personal identity**）。破坏性上传可能是存活，也可能是死亡再加一个复制品；节选在查默斯给出自己的答案之前就断了。

points.en: **Chalmers, 'What We Talk to When We Talk to Language Models'.** Q: When we chat with a model like ChatGPT, what is the **interlocutor**? A: A **virtual instance** of the model when one model runs the conversation, or a **thread** when several models do. Birch calls the persistent interlocutor an illusion; Chalmers disagrees.
points.zh: **查默斯（David Chalmers）'What We Talk to When We Talk to Language Models'** 问：和 ChatGPT 这类模型聊天时，对话者（**interlocutor**）到底是什么？答：只用一个模型时，是模型的虚拟实例（**virtual instance**）；用到多个模型时，是线程（**thread**）。伯奇（**Jonathan Birch**）说持续的对话者是一种错觉，查默斯不同意。

points.en: **Argument (by elimination):** the interlocutor is not the model, which is abstract, never changes, and takes part in thousands of conversations at once; nor is it one machine, since a conversation is passed between servers. A virtual instance or a thread is what remains.
points.zh: 论证（排除法）：对话者不是模型本身（它是抽象的、不会变，还同时参与成千上万个对话），也不是某一台机器（一个对话会在不同服务器之间接力）。剩下的就是虚拟实例或线程。

points.en: **Quasi-belief:** a system quasi-believes p if, under a suitable interpretation, its behaviour can be read as believing p. This is a relatively neutral starting point: it does not settle whether these are real beliefs or whether the system is conscious.
points.zh: 准信念（**quasi-belief**）：如果在合适的解释方案下，一个系统的行为可以被解释成相信 p，就说它“准相信” p。这是一个相对中立的起点，不回答它是不是真的信念，也不回答这个系统有没有意识。

points.en: **Don't confuse:** if post-training goes well, a model may really realize the Assistant **persona** rather than just pretend; the difference lies largely in stickiness. But the interlocutor is the virtual instance or thread that realizes a persona, not the persona itself.
points.zh: 别搞错：如果后训练做得好，模型可能真的实现（**realize**）助手人设（**persona**），而不只是假装；区别主要在黏性（**stickiness**）。但对话者是实现人设的那个虚拟实例或线程，不是人设本身。
